messages:
maria.g: FYI customer 'Neptune Labs' reporting sudden spike in 502s and a few 504s on hosted streaming endpoints since this morning. Started ~08:07 UTC. They said it began right after we rolled the session-affinity change to frontdoor.

maria.g: Example curl (non-streaming) returned 502 intermittently: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-llama\"`

maria.g: Error seen in client logs: `upstream prematurely closed connection` + `no healthy upstream` traces.

jon.sre: looking. can you drop the trace IDs/sample request IDs? I want to correlate with envoy logs.

maria.g: paste below — request-id: rq_2026_08_07_15A4, span: trace-9ab3. Also saw many `RST_STREAM` on the edge.

carla.eng: I pulled the edge proxy logs for those request-ids — lots of 502s with upstream status 0 and ECONNRESET to auth-cache (10.23.12.4:8080). Also seeing a pattern: connection pool churn and many new h2 streams. suspect keepalive/idle window mismatch after affinity toggle.

jon.sre: @carla.eng good catch. affinity change removed source-IP sticky routing; that increased upstream fanout which stressed the auth-cache's connection pool. auth-cache started refusing/closing which cascaded to edge returning 502s.

sam.support: Customer impact: 13% of streaming requests failed in last 30m, mostly long-lived streams. They flagged an SLA hit. They're asking for repro steps + ETA.

carla.eng: Repro steps I used: 1) start 50 concurrent streaming sessions with small frames, 2) toggle stickiness off at frontdoor, 3) observe RST_STREAM & 502s within 90s. I can attach a short script.

carla.eng: Script snippet:```bash
for i in $(seq 1 50); do 
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
    \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-llama\" &
done
wait
```

jon.sre: mitigation path: 1) temporarily re-enable session-affinity for the impacted pool (will reduce upstream churn) 2) increase auth-cache upstream keepalive and max_concurrent_streams, 3) add 30s ramp to health-checks. I'll open a quick runbook.

maria.g: can we short-circuit while we fix? e.g., fallback to a local auth cache replica per edge node?

carla.eng: We have a fallback in routing-policy — can route auth calls to local read-only replica. I'll prepare a one-liner to flip for eu1 pool. Expected to cut 502 rate by ~80%.

sre-bot: deploybot: rolling config change started by jon.sre to enable affinity rollback on frontdoor-eu1 at 15:09 UTC. Change ID cfg_183777_0.

jon.sre: deploying keepalive bump to auth-cache (tcp_keepalive: 75 -> 300) and max concurrent streams 100 -> 500. Will monitor.

maria.g: shared customer-facing note: "We're aware and have applied a mitigation that should restore >90% of streaming traffic. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with root cause and permanent fix." They asked for ETA on permanent fix.

carla.eng: root cause notes for postmortem: affinity removal increased fanout, auth-cache connection pool not sized for fanout increase, h2 connection/keepalive mismatch -> RST_STREAM & connection resets -> edge treats as upstream failure -> 502/504. Permanent fix options: resize auth-cache pool, add per-edge auth-cache shard, or keep affinity with smarter routing.

jon.sre: monitoring: dashboards updated, alert threshold lowered to 3% 502 rate for streaming endpoints. I'll keep watch for 2h.

sam.support: Customer notified at 15:25 UTC with the mitigation and timeline. I'll follow up with SLA calc. :thumbsup:

maria.g: thanks all. mark for incident PM and include reproduction script + sample logs in incident artifact.

carla.eng: +1. I'll open the postmortem ticket and copy the config diffs.

sre-bot: incident-manager: incident created INC-2026-6645 (priority P1) and assigned to eng-oncall.

jon.sre: marking this thread resolved for now — monitoring shows 502s back down to baseline (~0.6%). will reopen if it creeps. :eyes:
